title: Cap each parking visit on its own

blocks.text: The garage's barrier app charges a parked car in parts. Each time it settles a stretch of parked time, it calls `charge(visit, minutes)` on the car's tariff and books what comes back. A tariff has a price per started hour and a cap: however long a car stays, its visit never pays more than the cap in total.
`Garage` already holds the three tariffs with their prices and caps. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Garage.java`:

items: `Tariff.charge(visit, minutes)`: what this part of the visit costs, every started hour at the tariff's price, cut down to what is left of the visit's cap.

blocks.text: You may add to `Visit` whatever a visit needs. When you're done, every visit pays its started hours until it reaches its tariff's cap and nothing after that, whether it is the only car in the garage, follows a car that already hit the cap, or is parked at the same time as other cars on the same tariff. About six lines in total.

cases.says: each part of a visit costs its started hours at the tariff's price
a visit's parts add up to the cap at most, and a part after the cap costs nothing
a visit after another one reached the cap on the same tariff pays its own started hours in full
two visits charged alternately on the same tariff each keep their own total toward the cap

origin.section: A Constant's Data Goes Through the Constructor, So a New Constant Can't Leave It Out

concepts: A constant is one object shared by every caller, so per-use data such as a running total belongs in an object passed to the constant, not in a field on it.
